summary: Oglethorpe County tower in a Georgia lookout index at 34.00068,-83.01381; no source found on its build, staffing or condition today.

evidence.supports: Index entry: point peter, Oglethorpe County, coordinates 34.00068,-83.01381
Fire towers in Georgia date to the early 20th century; the count peaked at more than 200 in the 1960s
evidence.quote: The Peach State's use of fire towers dates to the early 20th century, with the count peaking at more than 200 in the 1960s

evidence.supports: 137 of the state's 144 still-existing towers were no longer staffed (2006)
evidence.quote: 137 of the state's 144 still-existing towers are no longer staffed.

evidence.supports: Auction sales; some towers sold for scrap metal or to hunting clubs or other groups
evidence.quote: The towers are being auctioned off - sold for scrap metal in some cases, or to hunting clubs or other groups.

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association identified 360 sites and former sites of Georgia's fire towers
evidence.quote: The Forest Fire Lookout Association has identified 360 sites and former sites of Georgia's fire towers.

sources.title: Fire towers are fading into history
sources.publisher: Savannah Morning News (Internet Archive copy of the 2006 article by Charles Cochran)

notes_for_editor: Only tower-specific source is one index line (name, county, coordinates, elevation 673 with no unit). It gives no build date, height, operator, status or access. Searches and cached NHLR/FFLOS pages found nothing specific to this tower, only genealogy and place-name pages. The index's elevation has no unit; 673 matches the record's 205.1 m only if read as feet. The BLL and gfc codes are not defined in any source found; the index gives this tower none. Story is short because the evidence is thin.
